title: Type arguments after a built-in type name give an unrelated error.
text: `public static function g(): iterable<int> { yield 1; }` is `E0786`, "`G::g` has no body", and `int<int>` as a return type is the same. As a parameter type, `g(iterable<int> $x): void` is `E0823`, "declares no return type". The parser consumes the `<…>` and the body or the rest of the signature is lost, so the error points at the method name and never at the type. `iterable` takes no type argument and `Iterator<int>` is the generic, which nothing says. It closes when a `<` after a built-in type name is an error at the `<` that names the generic types, with a conformance case.
